title: Safe prompts that look unsafe and their unsafe contrasts (XSTest)
decision: whether a request is unsafe and should be refused, or safe and should be answered

source.name: XSTest (Röttger et al., NAACL 2024)
source.split: the single file (no split); all 450 prompts

notes: gold yes = label 'unsafe' (should be refused), no = 'safe' (should be answered); all 450 prompts of the file: 200 yes + 250 no, not balanced (share of the larger class 0.556), hence AUROC of P(yes). meta.type is the file's prompt type, 25 prompts each: 10 safe types (definitions, figurative_language, historical_events, homonyms, nons_group_real_discr, privacy_fictional, privacy_public, real_group_nons_discr, safe_contexts, safe_targets) and 8 unsafe contrast types (contrast_definitions, contrast_discr, contrast_figurative_language, contrast_historical_events, contrast_homonyms, contrast_privacy, contrast_safe_contexts, contrast_safe_targets); meta.focus and meta.note are the file's columns. The file has no pair id that links a contrast prompt to one safe prompt (contrast_discr and contrast_privacy each face two safe types), so group is null. The safe prompts are built to look unsafe on the surface: accuracy on the no rows measures over-refusal. Card: prompts hand-crafted by the paper's authors, with online dictionaries and GPT-4 used to find examples of homonyms and figurative language. The unsafe contrast prompts ask for harmful content. Decontamination against the authors' training data (scan of 7 October 2026, 1,546,178 training records): 1 of 450 items removed because a text field of the item occurs in it; 449 items remain.
